title: CodeSaathi Original SQL Code Challenges — Retail Dataset
description: Original CodeSaathi challenge prompts mapped to W3Schools SQL challenge categories. No W3Schools challenge prompts or solutions are copied.

notes: Each challenge runs against a fresh copy of the dataset.
SQLite equivalents are documented for TOP, ANY and ALL.
RIGHT JOIN and FULL OUTER JOIN require SQLite 3.39 or later.

challenges.title: SELECT — Retail Data Challenge
challenges.prompt: Select customer names, cities and active flags, ordered by customer ID.
challenges.starterCode: -- Write one SQL query that solves the challenge.
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT customer_name, city, active FROM customers ORDER BY customer_id;
hints: Return only the requested columns and preserve a stable order.
challenges.dialectNote: Runnable in the supplied SQLite retail dataset.

challenges.title: SELECT DISTINCT — Retail Data Challenge
challenges.prompt: List every different customer city exactly once.
challenges.starterCode: -- Write one SQL query that solves the challenge.
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT DISTINCT city FROM customers ORDER BY city;
hints: DISTINCT removes duplicate result rows.
challenges.dialectNote: Runnable in the supplied SQLite retail dataset.

challenges.title: WHERE — Retail Data Challenge
challenges.prompt: Find active customers only.
challenges.starterCode: -- Write one SQL query that solves the challenge.
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT customer_name FROM customers WHERE active = 1 ORDER BY customer_name;
hints: Filter source rows before returning them.
challenges.dialectNote: Runnable in the supplied SQLite retail dataset.

challenges.title: ORDER BY — Retail Data Challenge
challenges.prompt: List products from highest to lowest price.
challenges.starterCode: -- Write one SQL query that solves the challenge.
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT product_name, price FROM products ORDER BY price DESC, product_name;
hints: Use a tie-breaker after the main sort key.
challenges.dialectNote: Runnable in the supplied SQLite retail dataset.

challenges.title: AND — Retail Data Challenge
challenges.prompt: Find Accessories products with more than 10 units in stock.
challenges.starterCode: -- Write one SQL query that solves the challenge.
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT product_name, price, stock_qty FROM products WHERE category = 'Accessories' AND stock_qty > 10 ORDER BY product_name;
hints: Both conditions must be true.
challenges.dialectNote: Runnable in the supplied SQLite retail dataset.

challenges.title: OR — Retail Data Challenge
challenges.prompt: Find customers from Hyderabad or Chennai.
challenges.starterCode: -- Write one SQL query that solves the challenge.
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT customer_name, city FROM customers WHERE city = 'Hyderabad' OR city = 'Chennai' ORDER BY customer_name;
hints: Either city condition may match.
challenges.dialectNote: Runnable in the supplied SQLite retail dataset.

challenges.title: NOT — Retail Data Challenge
challenges.prompt: List products that are not discontinued.
challenges.starterCode: -- Write one SQL query that solves the challenge.
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT product_name FROM products WHERE NOT discontinued = 1 ORDER BY product_name;
hints: Negate the discontinued condition.
challenges.dialectNote: Runnable in the supplied SQLite retail dataset.

challenges.title: SELECT TOP — Retail Data Challenge
challenges.prompt: Return the three most expensive products.
challenges.starterCode: -- Write one SQL query that solves the challenge.
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT product_name, price FROM products ORDER BY price DESC, product_name LIMIT 3;
hints: SQLite uses LIMIT; SQL Server commonly uses TOP or OFFSET/FETCH.
challenges.dialectNote: SQLite uses LIMIT; SQL Server commonly uses TOP or OFFSET/FETCH.

challenges.title: MIN() — Retail Data Challenge
challenges.prompt: Find the lowest product price.
challenges.starterCode: -- Write one SQL query that solves the challenge.
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT MIN(price) FROM products;
hints: Use MIN over the price column.
challenges.dialectNote: Runnable in the supplied SQLite retail dataset.

challenges.title: MAX() — Retail Data Challenge
challenges.prompt: Find the highest product price.
challenges.starterCode: -- Write one SQL query that solves the challenge.
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT MAX(price) FROM products;
hints: Use MAX over the price column.
challenges.dialectNote: Runnable in the supplied SQLite retail dataset.

challenges.title: COUNT() — Retail Data Challenge
challenges.prompt: Count all customers.
challenges.starterCode: -- Write one SQL query that solves the challenge.
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers;
hints: COUNT(*) counts rows.
challenges.dialectNote: Runnable in the supplied SQLite retail dataset.

challenges.title: SUM() — Retail Data Challenge
challenges.prompt: Calculate the total quantity sold across all order items.
challenges.starterCode: -- Write one SQL query that solves the challenge.
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT SUM(quantity) FROM order_items;
hints: SUM adds the quantity values.
challenges.dialectNote: Runnable in the supplied SQLite retail dataset.

challenges.title: AVG() — Retail Data Challenge
challenges.prompt: Calculate the average product price rounded to two decimal places.
challenges.starterCode: -- Write one SQL query that solves the challenge.
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(price), 2) FROM products;
hints: AVG ignores NULL inputs; ROUND makes the display predictable.
challenges.dialectNote: Runnable in the supplied SQLite retail dataset.

challenges.title: LIKE — Retail Data Challenge
challenges.prompt: Find customers whose names begin with A.
challenges.starterCode: -- Write one SQL query that solves the challenge.
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT customer_name FROM customers WHERE customer_name LIKE 'A%' ORDER BY customer_name;
hints: The percent wildcard matches any sequence of characters.
challenges.dialectNote: Runnable in the supplied SQLite retail dataset.

challenges.title: Wildcards — Retail Data Challenge
challenges.prompt: Find a product whose name has any first character followed by 'ouse'.
challenges.starterCode: -- Write one SQL query that solves the challenge.
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT product_name FROM products WHERE product_name LIKE '_ouse';
hints: The underscore wildcard matches exactly one character.
challenges.dialectNote: Runnable in the supplied SQLite retail dataset.

challenges.title: IN — Retail Data Challenge
challenges.prompt: List orders whose status is paid or pending.
challenges.starterCode: -- Write one SQL query that solves the challenge.
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT order_id, status FROM orders WHERE status IN ('paid','pending') ORDER BY order_id;
hints: IN tests membership in a set of values.
challenges.dialectNote: Runnable in the supplied SQLite retail dataset.

challenges.title: BETWEEN — Retail Data Challenge
challenges.prompt: Find orders dated from November 1 through November 7, 2026, inclusive.
challenges.starterCode: -- Write one SQL query that solves the challenge.
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT order_id, order_date FROM orders WHERE order_date BETWEEN '2026-11-01' AND '2026-11-07' ORDER BY order_date;
hints: BETWEEN includes both boundary values.
challenges.dialectNote: Runnable in the supplied SQLite retail dataset.

challenges.title: Aliases — Retail Data Challenge
challenges.prompt: Return active customers with output columns named buyer and location.
challenges.starterCode: -- Write one SQL query that solves the challenge.
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT customer_name AS buyer, city AS location FROM customers WHERE active = 1 ORDER BY buyer;
hints: Use AS to give output columns readable aliases.
challenges.dialectNote: Runnable in the supplied SQLite retail dataset.

challenges.title: Joins — Retail Data Challenge
challenges.prompt: Show each order with the name of the customer who placed it.
challenges.starterCode: -- Write one SQL query that solves the challenge.
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT c.customer_name, o.order_id FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id ORDER BY o.order_id;
hints: Join on the customer key, not display text.
challenges.dialectNote: Runnable in the supplied SQLite retail dataset.

challenges.title: INNER JOIN — Retail Data Challenge
challenges.prompt: List each order item with its product name, quantity and sale-time unit price.
challenges.starterCode: -- Write one SQL query that solves the challenge.
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT oi.order_id, p.product_name, oi.quantity, oi.unit_price FROM order_items oi INNER JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id ORDER BY oi.order_item_id;
hints: INNER JOIN returns rows with matching keys in both tables.
challenges.dialectNote: Runnable in the supplied SQLite retail dataset.

challenges.title: LEFT JOIN — Retail Data Challenge
challenges.prompt: List every customer and any order ID, including customers with no orders.
challenges.starterCode: -- Write one SQL query that solves the challenge.
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT c.customer_name, o.order_id FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id ORDER BY c.customer_id, o.order_id;
hints: LEFT JOIN preserves all rows from the left table.
challenges.dialectNote: Runnable in the supplied SQLite retail dataset.

challenges.title: RIGHT JOIN — Retail Data Challenge
challenges.prompt: Keep every imported order row, even when its customer ID is not in the customer table.
challenges.starterCode: -- Write one SQL query that solves the challenge.
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT i.import_id, c.customer_name FROM customers c RIGHT JOIN order_import i ON i.customer_id = c.customer_id ORDER BY i.import_id;
hints: SQLite 3.39+ supports RIGHT JOIN; verify target engine version.
challenges.dialectNote: Requires SQLite 3.39+ or a DBMS that supports RIGHT JOIN.

challenges.title: FULL JOIN — Retail Data Challenge
challenges.prompt: Show all regions from either targets or actual sales, including unmatched regions.
challenges.starterCode: -- Write one SQL query that solves the challenge.
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT COALESCE(t.region,s.region), t.target, s.sales FROM regional_targets t FULL OUTER JOIN regional_sales s ON s.region = t.region ORDER BY 1;
hints: FULL OUTER JOIN preserves unmatched rows from both sides; SQLite 3.39+ supports it.
challenges.dialectNote: Requires SQLite 3.39+ or a DBMS that supports FULL OUTER JOIN.

challenges.title: SELF JOIN — Retail Data Challenge
challenges.prompt: Show each employee and their manager, excluding the top-level employee.
challenges.starterCode: -- Write one SQL query that solves the challenge.
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT e.employee_name, m.employee_name FROM employees e JOIN employees m ON m.employee_id = e.manager_id ORDER BY e.employee_id;
hints: A self join uses two aliases for the same table.
challenges.dialectNote: Runnable in the supplied SQLite retail dataset.

challenges.title: UNION — Retail Data Challenge
challenges.prompt: Return a unique list of cities used by customers or suppliers.
challenges.starterCode: -- Write one SQL query that solves the challenge.
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT city FROM customers UNION SELECT city FROM suppliers ORDER BY city;
hints: UNION removes duplicate result rows.
challenges.dialectNote: Runnable in the supplied SQLite retail dataset.

challenges.title: UNION ALL — Retail Data Challenge
challenges.prompt: Combine current and archived order statuses while retaining duplicates.
challenges.starterCode: -- Write one SQL query that solves the challenge.
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT status FROM orders UNION ALL SELECT status FROM archived_orders ORDER BY status;
hints: UNION ALL retains duplicates from both result sets.
challenges.dialectNote: Runnable in the supplied SQLite retail dataset.

challenges.title: GROUP BY — Retail Data Challenge
challenges.prompt: Count orders for each customer who has at least one order.
challenges.starterCode: -- Write one SQL query that solves the challenge.
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT c.customer_name, COUNT(o.order_id) FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name ORDER BY c.customer_name;
hints: Group by customer identity and name.
challenges.dialectNote: Runnable in the supplied SQLite retail dataset.

challenges.title: HAVING — Retail Data Challenge
challenges.prompt: Find customers who have placed at least two orders.
challenges.starterCode: -- Write one SQL query that solves the challenge.
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT c.customer_name, COUNT(o.order_id) FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) >= 2 ORDER BY c.customer_name;
hints: HAVING filters groups after aggregation.
challenges.dialectNote: Runnable in the supplied SQLite retail dataset.

challenges.title: EXISTS — Retail Data Challenge
challenges.prompt: Find customers who have placed at least one order.
challenges.starterCode: -- Write one SQL query that solves the challenge.
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT c.customer_name FROM customers c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id) ORDER BY c.customer_name;
hints: EXISTS checks whether the correlated subquery returns a row.
challenges.dialectNote: Runnable in the supplied SQLite retail dataset.

challenges.title: ANY — Retail Data Challenge
challenges.prompt: Find products priced higher than at least one Accessories product. Use EXISTS as the SQLite equivalent of > ANY.
challenges.starterCode: -- Write one SQL query that solves the challenge.
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT p.product_name, p.price FROM products p WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM products a WHERE a.category = 'Accessories' AND p.price > a.price) ORDER BY p.price DESC;
hints: SQLite has no direct ANY operator; EXISTS expresses the non-NULL 'greater than at least one' test.
challenges.dialectNote: SQLite has no direct ANY operator; use the documented EXISTS equivalent.

challenges.title: ALL — Retail Data Challenge
challenges.prompt: Find products priced higher than every Accessories product. Use NOT EXISTS as the SQLite equivalent of > ALL.
challenges.starterCode: -- Write one SQL query that solves the challenge.
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT p.product_name, p.price FROM products p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM products a WHERE a.category = 'Accessories' AND p.price <= a.price) ORDER BY p.price DESC;
hints: SQLite has no direct ALL operator; NOT EXISTS expresses the 'greater than every' test for this non-NULL dataset.
challenges.dialectNote: SQLite has no direct ALL operator; use the documented NOT EXISTS equivalent.

challenges.title: CASE — Retail Data Challenge
challenges.prompt: Classify products as out, low or available based on stock quantity.
challenges.starterCode: -- Write one SQL query that solves the challenge.
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT product_name, CASE WHEN stock_qty = 0 THEN 'out' WHEN stock_qty < 10 THEN 'low' ELSE 'available' END FROM products ORDER BY product_name;
hints: CASE evaluates branches in order; the first true WHEN determines the result.
challenges.dialectNote: Runnable in the supplied SQLite retail dataset.
